segments.text: Seventeen days after a mine collapses, a drill comes back up with a note tied to it.
In red ink, it says: we are fine in the shelter, the thirty-three of us.
Thirty-three miners, seven hundred metres down. For seventeen days nobody knew if they were alive. Seven drill holes had missed.
Their food was meant for a couple of days. So each man got two spoonfuls of tuna, every other day.
But that hole fits a note, not a man. Drilling one wide enough takes seven more weeks.
Then a steel capsule, barely wider than their shoulders, goes down. One man at a time, up through solid rock.
In under a day, all thirty-three are out. Sixty-nine days underground.
I was wrong. Their foreman rode up last. Would you have waited? And the rescue began
